issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s clear and non-bona-fide denial of the landlord’s title during a rent-control eviction proceeding may itself support eviction in that proceeding, even if the denial occurred after the proceeding began.
material_facts: The tenant alleged in the counter to the eviction petition that the premises were trust property and that the landlord had no personal or proprietary interest in them.
The Rent Controller found that the tenant’s denial of the landlord’s title was not bona fide, and the High Court upheld eviction on that ground.
The denial was made during the eviction proceeding; the landlord had also sought eviction on the ground of bona fide personal requirement.
issues.conclusion: The denial of title did not have to precede the eviction petition. A qualifying denial made during the proceeding could be relied on as a ground for eviction in that same proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960 prohibits eviction except in accordance with that section or sections 12 and 13; section 10(2)(vi) expressly makes a tenant’s denial of the landlord’s title, if not bona fide, a ground for eviction. Under V. Dhanapal Chettiar v. Yesodai Ammal, the Rent Acts govern recovery of possession on their specified grounds and displace the need to apply the Transfer of Property Act’s rules on termination of a lease. Kundan Mal v. Gurudutta did not hold that denial must precede the eviction proceeding. Sada Ram v. Gajjan Shiama, Shiv Parshad v. Smt. Shila Rani, and Machavaram Venkata Narayana Rao v. Sarvepalli Narayana Rao Sarada support relying on a denial made in the tenant’s written statement in the same proceeding. A court may also consider subsequent events in moulding relief.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The landlord sought eviction of a tenant in a proceeding governed by rent-control rules.
predicates.tenant_denied_landlord_title_during_proc: The tenant disputed the landlord’s title in the course of the eviction proceeding.
predicates.denial_was_clear_and_not_bona_fide: The tenant’s denial of the landlord’s title was clear and was found not to be bona fide.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding is governed by rent-control rules and the tenant clearly and non-bona-fide denies the landlord’s title during that proceeding, the denial may support eviction in that same proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who had notice of an unpleaded title-denial ground, proceeded to trial on an issue framed about it, and did not object to the issue cannot later challenge eviction on the ground that the petition did not plead that ground.
material_facts: The eviction petition did not plead the tenant’s denial of title as a ground that arose during the proceeding.
The Rent Controller framed an issue about whether the tenant’s denial of the landlord’s title was bona fide.
The parties proceeded to trial on that issue, and the tenant knew the ground alleged against him but did not object to the framing of the issue.
issues.conclusion: Although amendment of the eviction petition would normally have been required to add the later-arising ground, the tenant could not complain of the omission after proceeding to trial on the issue without objection.
issues.legal_principle: The Court accepted that a landlord would normally need to amend the eviction petition to plead a ground arising after filing. But where the decision-maker frames the issue, the tenant has notice and the parties try the issue without objection, the tenant cannot later contend that relief was unavailable because the ground was not pleaded. The ruling applies the procedural circumstances of the case; no earlier case was cited for this point.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and adjudicator_framed_unpleaded_title_denial_issue and tenant_had_notice_and_contested_issue and tenant_made_no_objection_to_issue

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The landlord sought eviction of a tenant in a proceeding governed by rent-control rules.
predicates.adjudicator_framed_unpleaded_title_denia: The decision-maker framed an issue about the tenant’s denial of title even though that ground was not pleaded in the eviction petition.
predicates.tenant_had_notice_and_contested_issue: The tenant knew that the denial of title was alleged and the parties proceeded to trial on that issue.
predicates.tenant_made_no_objection_to_issue: The tenant did not object to the issue being framed on the ground that the eviction petition had not pleaded it.

issues.definition: When the decision-maker frames an unpleaded title-denial issue in a rent-control eviction proceeding and the tenant knows of and contests it without objection, the tenant cannot later challenge eviction for lack of pleading.
